To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the forthcoming multi- and hyper-spectral satellite systems Sentinel-2 and EnMAP are able to produce local timber volume distribution maps for Norway spruce in the German federal state of Rheinland-Palatinate, and that the k-NN algorithm performs slightly better than PISR.

(i) The forthcoming multi- and hyper-spectral satellite systems are suitable for providing spatially distributed information on timber volume of Norway Spruce, (ii) the Sentinel-2 system is more suitable for producing maps of timber volume in higher geometric resolution and EnMAP for providing complementary information on biophysical conditions, and (iii) the k-NN algorithm is more accurate for estimating Norway Spruce timber volume compared to PLSR.
both Sentinel-2 and EnMAP can be used to support local forest operations, but EnMAP will provide complementary information on biophysical conditions.

the development of a spatially explicit forest inventory concept that combines the advantages of statistical sampling and Earth observation.
a first step towards a fully integrated approach of terrestrial sampling and Earth observation to support operational forest management.
the question of how future satellite systems will be able to support forest management in the near future.
